title: Pending Home Sales Index (NAR, November 2026 data) — the contracts-signed leading half of the corridor's residential pair, 10:00 a.m. ET on December opex eve
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nar.realtor/newsroom/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule (302 -> /press-releases/..., HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-06) and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "DECEMBER | Thu., Dec. 17 | November Pending Home Sales Index" under the standing note "All releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern Time". The .docx carries the full year; the live page carries September onward and agrees row for row. Promoted from the `EST:` proposal filed 2026-09-06 by the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 sweep, on the same precedent that lane used (challenger-job-cuts-2026-09-03: a private publisher's own release carried IR:/confirmed — NAR produces this series, it does not report someone else's). Corroborated on execution rather than only on schedule: NAR's own July-data press release, /newsroom/NAR-Pending-Home-Sales-Report-Shows-2-3-Decrease-in-July, carries <time>August 18, 2026</time>, exactly the schedule's "Tue., Aug. 18 | July Pending Home Sales Index" row. ONE conflicting NAR surface, recorded not hidden: the pending-home-sales statistics page's own "Next release" note reads "Pending Home Sales for August 2026 will be released on Thursday, September 10, 2026" — that is the EXISTING-home sales date from the same schedule, and the same page carries two further stale artifacts (a day-20 release cadence NAR abandoned in January 2026, and an infographic dated July 16 describing July data). The schedule and the .docx govern; the resolution is registered as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-12-17-1, scored 2026-09-17. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The leading half of the residential pair this corridor already tracks: existing-home sales counts CLOSINGS, so the 12-09 print reports contracts signed 30-60 days earlier, while the PHSI counts the contracts themselves — NAR's own words, "a leading indicator of housing activity... generally leads Existing-Home Sales by a month or two." Both prints report reference month NOVEMBER 2026; they describe different cohorts of the same month, so 12-17 is the forward read the 12-09 print structurally cannot give. TWO measured findings from this event's initial research (2026-09-06), both narrowing rather than widening what it is good for. (1) NO NOWCAST CHANNEL — the open question the proposing lane flagged is closed, negatively. GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx's Residential sheet carries six leaves (Permanent-site, Manufactured homes, Dormitories, Brokerage commissions, Improvements, Residential equipment) and none is a pending-sales variable; 'pending home' appears 0 times across the workbook's 3,665 shared strings and 14 comment files, against 22 distinct strings naming existing-home sales, 34 naming housing starts and 42 naming new-home sales. The reason is structural: GDP books the brokerage commission at CLOSING, and a signed contract is not a transaction. Belt and suspenders — GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx puts the 2026-12-17 vintage at 08:30 ("Housing starts, Import and export prices"), NINETY MINUTES BEFORE this 10:00 print, so that vintage could not carry it even if the model wanted it. (2) THE TAPE IS INERT AND THE SLOT IS NOT — on the 8 realized 2026 PHSI release days the print's own 10:00-11:00 hour takes a median 33.9% of ITB's session range against a 35.3% baseline (723 sessions 2023-10-09 -> 2026-09-04, p=0.79), 30.8% vs 37.1% for XHB (p=0.36) and 39.5% vs 39.9% for SPY (p=0.96) — exactly ordinary. A whole-session read looks hot (ITB median |open->close| 1.825% vs 0.893% baseline, p=0.039 with the FOMC day removed) and that is a CALENDAR ARTIFACT, not the release: 4 of the 8 dates carry a homebuilder 8-K Item 2.02 within one day (DHI 2026-01-20 and 2026-04-21, NVR 2026-04-22, TOL 2026-05-19 and 2026-08-18) and a 5th, 2026-06-17, is an FOMC SEP decision day; the 8 existing-home-sales dates in the same year carry ZERO such collisions. NAR's day-16-to-21 PHSI slot sits inside the builder reporting window; its day-9-to-14 EHS slot sits before it. Impact stays `low` and `symbols: []` on the same basis as the sibling: no house playbook is macro- or housing-keyed and no instrument attaches. Date `confirmed` licenses nothing; the ledger's call is stand aside on every horizon. Full research: docs/research/events/pending-home-sales-2026-12-17.md
